messages:
Nadia Rao: Pushed a new mock for the suppression scheduler. Main ideas: weekly recurring windows, one-off maintenance, and a calendar heatmap for quick scanning. Uploading artboards now.
James Kim: Nice. Does the heatmap show team-local times or a single org timezone?
Nadia Rao: By default it shows the team's primary timezone. There's a toggle to render everything in UTC or in a chosen fixed timezone. Preview also has a small banner showing which timezone is active.
Elliot Shaw: Edge case: DST transitions. If a weekly window is "Sun 02:00-04:00" in a DST-observing locale, the duration shifts. How are we representing that?
Priya Menon: We should store windows as local wall-clock times + tz identifier so the UI can display exactly what users expect after DST flips. Also surface a DST warning in the review step: "This window overlaps a DST change on Nov 3, duration will be 3h instead of 2h."
Nadia Rao: Agreed. I'll add a small inline tooltip with that exact phrasing and a link to help docs.
a11y-bot: Accessibility note: the calendar heatmap must be navigable by keyboard and announce the date, window type, and status (active/recurring/one-off). Use aria-describedby to link to the summary.
James Kim: For the inline editor, I'm proposing two modes: "Quick" (drag on calendar, simple start/end) and "Advanced" (cron-like recurrence rules). Quick for most users, advanced for infra teams.
Priya Menon: Copy nits: instead of "Quick" call it "Simple schedule" and instead of "Advanced" use "Custom recurrence". Also change microcopy from "suppresses alerts" to "pauses notifications" — clearer for non-ops folks.
Elliot Shaw: Preview feature request: simulate a 48-hour window around the scheduled maintenance and show which alerts would be muted vs which would break through (if route has "override" flags). Animated timeline helps.
Nadia Rao: I mocked a short simulation pane that shows sample alerts moving along the timeline and flags where suppression applies. It also highlights conflicts: e.g., "Route A has a higher-priority override at 01:15 which bypasses suppression."
James Kim: When creating org-level windows, we need a clear visual for "Inherited" vs "Local" schedules. Proposal: badges (Inherited / Local) and an "Expand" to show source. If org-locked, show lock icon and a tooltip: "This schedule is managed by org settings."
Priya Menon: If it's org-locked, route owners should be able to request an exception. A small CTA: "Request exception" opens a lightweight modal to send to admins. Include fields: reason, duration, and urgency.
a11y-bot: Ensure the "Request exception" workflow is accessible: focus trap in modal, label each input, provide success/error notifications via aria-live.
Elliot Shaw: Conflict detection UX: when a user creates a new window that overlaps an existing one with different semantics (e.g., one is "silence all" and other is "silence non-critical"), warn them and surface an auto-resolve suggestion: "Merge as most-restrictive" or "Keep both".
Nadia Rao: I'll add a small diff-like panel showing both rules side-by-side and a recommended resolution. Users can accept or edit.
James Kim: Keyboard accessibility for drag: allow keyboard to create and resize windows using arrow keys +/- while focused, and show live textual feedback ("Window: Tue 22:00 - Wed 02:00, length 4h").
Priya Menon: Microcopy tweak: main CTA should read "Save schedule" not "Create" because users sometimes edit existing ones. Secondary CTA: "Save & notify" to alert stakeholders.
Elliot Shaw: Can we include a small cost impact note for suppression windows? e.g., "Suppressing SMS reduces expected notifications by ~X%" — helps teams balance on-call coverage vs cost.
Nadia Rao: I'll add a cost estimator chip that appears when sms/pager entries are part of the affected routes. Tooltip explains the estimate assumptions.
a11y-bot: Color use: don't rely on green/red only. For heatmap intensity, provide pattern fills for users with color vision deficiency and include numeric labels on hover/focus.
James Kim: One more: bulk edit. Teams want to apply the same window to multiple routes. Add a multi-select and preview summary: "Applying to 12 routes: 3 critical, 9 non-critical."
Priya Menon: Bulk apply should also show which routes will be impacted by org-level locks and surface a list of lock blockers.
Nadia Rao: Great. I'll iterate the mocks with these changes: DST warnings, request-exception flow, conflict diff panel, keyboard/resizing affordances, simple vs custom modes, cost chip, and bulk-edit UX.
design-bot: Reminder: design review Thursday 10am PT. Please update Figma and the spec doc before then.
James Kim: Will review the mock timeline and test DST scenarios.
Elliot Shaw: I'll draft the help doc language for DST and recurrence semantics.
Priya Menon: I'll proof microcopy and produce final strings for localization.
Nadia Rao: Uploading new artboards: https://drive.redwood/design/suppression-scheduler-iter1. Thanks all!
